_comment: The only per-repo file in this skill. SKILL.md and repos.md are identical
across every repo that uses /ai-dev — when you copy the skill to another
project, edit this file and nothing else.
'toolkit' is the shared UI library this repo consumes from sources via a
relative path. Set it to null in a repo that has no such dependency.
'dataDirRoot' is where each unit's throwaway app data lives: SKILL.md
substitutes {dataDir} = <dataDirRoot>/<unit key> (the epic's key for an
epic unit) into runInstructions. It must be outside the home directory —
No Claude Code sandbox is configured for this repo: it was tried (TRF-11)
and Electron aborts inside it (Seatbelt denies its Mach port check-in), and
pkill cannot list processes. The run script is the only guard.
runInstructions: You may launch the app, but ONLY isolated, and ONLY through the run script:
LUNARBOR_LOCAL_DATA={dataDir} scripts/ai-dev-run.sh {port} {dataDir}
{dataDir} is this unit's own data directory — shared by every child of an epic,
so each child sees the vault its predecessors left behind. LUNARBOR_LOCAL_DATA
moves Electron's userData (and with it the single-instance lock) to
{dataDir}/electron, and the themes, UI-settings and layout files out of
~/Library/Application Support/Darkness into {dataDir}. Leave LUNARBOR_VAULT
unset: the vault is then {dataDir}/vault. Without isolation a launch opens the
maintainer's REAL notes at ~/lunarbor-db, whose 5-second autosave writes back
whatever your branch does to them, and collides with the maintainer's own
running app.
The script enforces this rather than trusting you. It REFUSES to start (exit 2,
nothing launched) when LUNARBOR_LOCAL_DATA is unset, relative or under your home
directory, when LUNARBOR_VAULT points anywhere but {dataDir}/vault, when the
port is already taken, or when the Electron resources are not built. Never
work around a refusal: never run ./gradlew electron:run, scripts/run.sh, `npm
start` or node_modules/.bin/electron directly. A refusal means fix the
environment, not bypass the script.
Build once (repeat after each change; append the -Plunula.toolkit.path property
your brief gives you, as on every Gradle call):
./gradlew :electron:npmInstall :electron:copyWebBundle :electron:copyMainBundle
The script launches the app in the background and returns once it is up. It
prints the main process's two startup lines, which must read:
==> Vault: {dataDir}/vault (LUNARBOR_LOCAL_DATA)
==> Data: {dataDir} (LUNARBOR_LOCAL_DATA)
It checks them itself and stops the run, exiting non-zero, if they differ or if
the app dies before CDP answers. Quote the two lines in your PR's Verification
section. The app's output is in {dataDir}/electron-run.log.
To start from seeded content instead of an empty vault, run BEFORE launching:
python3 scripts/seed-vault.py --vault {dataDir}/vault
Drive it over CDP on port {port} as the /verify skill describes
(curl -s http://localhost:{port}/json, Runtime.evaluate, Page.captureScreenshot,
Input.dispatch*). Saved notes land as .md files under {dataDir}/vault.
Stop what you started: pkill -f -- "--remote-debugging-port={port}". That flag
is unique to your unit, so it cannot reach another ticket's window or the
maintainer's app. Never pkill Electron or Lunarbor by name. Stop the app
before you return: the next child of your epic launches on the same port.
scripts/wipe-vault.sh and scripts/seed-vault.py take the vault path as an
argument; always pass {dataDir}/vault explicitly.
Also verify without the app wherever you can:
· The configured build, which compiles every target and runs the tests.
· Unit tests in client/src/commonTest (SubtreeCodecTest, FolderStorageTest,
InlineMarkdownTokenizerTest, …). Everything below the View layer is
commonMain, so prefer adding a test that pins the ticket's behaviour — it
is the strongest verification this repo can offer.
State in the PR's Verification section exactly which flows you exercised in the
running app and which you could not, and list what a human should still click
through.
